sections.h2: Oman VAT and Compliance in ERPNext
sections.intro: Oman introduced VAT at 5% in April 2021. ERPNext Oman VAT setups follow Oman Tax Authority rules:

items.text: Standard rate of 5%, with zero-rated and exempt supplies as separate tax templates
Tax invoices with your VAT number, the buyer's VAT number where required, and Arabic text
Reverse charge on imported services and goods, posted automatically
VAT return figures prepared for filing with the Oman Tax Authority

outro.text: We test every tax template against real invoices from your business before go-live, including credit notes, discounts and mixed-rate invoices, so the first return after launch matches your accountant's figures.

outro.html: For official guidance, see the Oman Tax Authority.

paragraphs.text: Fawtara is the Oman Tax Authority's e-invoicing programme. The authority has opened its portal for service provider registration and has started notifying selected taxpayers, with the next phase expected to begin in the first quarter of 2027. Businesses that are notified will need to issue structured e-invoices through an approved route.

ERPNext Fawtara readiness work starts now: we clean customer VAT data, standardise invoice fields and plan the connection. ERPNext Fawtara integration will then link your invoices to the approved provider once the technical rules are final. Our ERPNext e-invoicing Oman projects are tested before your notified start date. An ERPNext implementation company Oman clients hire should track these dates for you, and we review them every quarter.

The Omani rial is divided into 1,000 baisa, so prices, taxes and totals need three decimal places. Many systems built for two decimals create rounding errors that build up over thousands of invoices, which is why any ERPNext implementation company Oman clients hire should set the currency precision before importing a single record. ERPNext OMR accounting is set to three decimals throughout, from item prices to VAT and bank reconciliation, so your totals match to the baisa.

sections.h2: Payroll, WPS and Social Protection Fund

paragraphs.html: Oman's Wage Protection System requires private-sector salaries to be paid through banks, with coverage expanded in phases through 2025 and full compliance expected from 2026. ERPNext's HR app calculates salaries, allowances and deductions, then produces the salary file your bank needs. Social Protection Fund contributions are tracked for each Omani employee, and end-of-service benefits for non-Omani staff are accrued monthly. Omanisation reports show your nationality mix by role and department. Visa, labour card and resident card expiry dates trigger reminders well before renewal, and leave balances are visible to each employee on mobile. For the full setup, see ERPNext HR and payroll for the GCC.

rows: Multi-currency buying, landed cost and stock across warehouses

paragraphs.text: ERPNext for Oman traders focuses on landed cost and stock control. ERPNext for Oman contractors relies on project budgets and retention tracking. Our ERPNext solutions Oman clients all use the same core system, configured for their sector.

Sohar, Duqm and Salalah host some of the region's busiest ports and free zones, and many Omani firms run logistics, warehousing or re-export businesses around them. ERPNext tracks goods by container and shipment, adds freight and clearing costs to stock, and separates free zone entities from mainland companies while still giving owners one group view. An ERPNext implementation company Oman logistics firms hire should understand these flows, because margin is often lost in the costs between ship and shelf.

Many Omani businesses run branches in several governorates. Each branch can have its own warehouse, cost centre and sales team, with stock transfers recorded by vehicle and driver. Management sees sales, stock and receivables for every branch in one report, without waiting for spreadsheets from each location.

paragraphs.html: Most Oman clients come from Tally, QuickBooks or spreadsheets. We move customers, suppliers, items, opening balances and open invoices, with VAT numbers checked for every record, and your old system stays live until the trial balance matches. An ERPNext implementation company Oman finance teams trust should finish every migration with a signed balance check. See ERPNext data migration.

items.q: Is ERPNext ready for Oman e-invoicing?
items.a: ERPNext produces structured invoice data and already connects to e-invoicing platforms elsewhere in the Gulf. We prepare your data and invoice fields now, then connect to the approved route once Fawtara's technical rules are final for your group.
Yes. ERPNext can be set to three decimal places for prices, taxes and totals, so amounts match to the baisa. We configure this at the start, because changing it later is harder.

items.q: Does ERPNext support Oman VAT at 5%?
items.a: Yes. We set up standard, zero-rated and exempt supplies, reverse charge and Arabic tax invoices, then prepare VAT return figures for filing with the Oman Tax Authority.

items.q: Can ERPNext produce WPS salary files?
items.a: Yes. ERPNext calculates salaries and produces the salary file your bank needs for WPS, along with Social Protection Fund contributions for Omani staff.

items.q: How long does an ERPNext project take in Oman?
items.a: A single company usually goes live in 8–12 weeks. Groups with several branches take 12–16 weeks. A good ERPNext implementation company Oman clients hire will give these dates in writing before work starts.

items.q: What does an ERPNext project cost in Oman?
items.a: The price depends on users, branches, modules and payroll size. ERPNext itself has no licence fee. After a short discovery call, an ERPNext implementation company Oman businesses can trust should send a fixed quote with every line item listed, and ours does.

items.q: Can you support us from India?
items.a: Yes. Kochi is 1.5 hours ahead of Muscat, so our working day overlaps fully with yours. Most work runs remotely, with on-site visits when the project needs them.
